source: MAFF Department of Agricultural Extension / ASPIRE Project, IFAD-funded - "បច្ចេកទេសដាំដុះក្រូចពោធិ៍សាត់ដែលធន់ទៅនឹងការប្រែប្រួលអាកាសធាតុ / Climate Resilient Orange Growing Technique", Nov 2018, 23pp
text:
This ASPIRE/IFAD-funded guide presents growing techniques for Pursat orange (ក្រូចពោធិសាត់) adapted to a changing and less predictable climate. It was developed to help farmers keep orchards productive as rainfall patterns become less reliable and temperatures more extreme, building on the same basic Pursat orange growing knowledge as the earlier MAFF extension bulletin but adding more specific guidance on water-saving irrigation, propagation, and orchard economics.

The guide reiterates that suitable land should have well-draining soil with a pH around 6.5, should not be prone to waterlogging, and should have dependable access to water for irrigation, since resilience to climate stress starts with choosing the right site.
